comparison: Both address EGFR activation experiments (C30-C34, C74). OpenEval finds the data SUPPORTED with appropriate controls and statistical significance. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, questioning why EGFR activation (4%) produces lower mitotic percentages than downstream effectors Pointed/Ras (11%) and whether EGFR is truly the 'master regulator'.

Both evaluate G-TRACE lineage tracing for transdifferentiation (C40-C42). OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED as direct proof of cell fate conversion. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY about why EGFR is more effective at transdifferentiation than at driving mitosis compared to Pointed/Ras, requesting speculation on this discrepancy.

Both address loss-of-function experiments and dpERK quantification (C44-C46, C52-C55). OpenEval finds convergent evidence SUPPORTED for active EGFR inhibition. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, requesting additional dpERK staining for Sprouty/PTEN knockdowns and compound knockdown experiments to clarify mechanisms.

Both evaluate Argos knockdown experiments (C59-C60). OpenEval finds the data SUPPORTED showing non-cell-autonomous regulation. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, requesting dpERK staining to confirm MAPK activation and questioning the differential interplay between EGFR ligands and Argos in different cell types.

Both address dpERK upregulation after CySC ablation (C62-C64). Both evaluations agree this finding is SUPPORTED with appropriate quantification and controls. This represents strong concordance between OpenEval and peer reviewers.

Both evaluate gene dosage experiments showing EGFR's role in recovery (C65-C68, C77). Both find the evidence SUPPORTED with appropriate statistics. OpenEval notes incomplete block suggests other pathways may be involved, which peer reviewers accept without challenge.

Both address EGFR's role in ectopic niche formation (C71-C73, C89-C90). OpenEval finds the data SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers express strong UNCERTAINTY, with Reviewer 1 challenging the negative conclusion, noting the null hypothesis was not rejected and requesting further data collection and statistical analyses.

Both address the negative result that EGFR activation alone doesn't cause ectopic niches (C73, C93-C94). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED as evidence for separable processes. Peer reviewers also find this SUPPORTED without challenge, though R8 questions the broader conclusion about EGFR's non-involvement.

Both evaluate negative results for JAK/STAT pathway (C37). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED as evidence for active suppression model. Peer reviewers also find this SUPPORTED without raising concerns about the negative results.

Both evaluate negative Notch results (C38). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED, contrasting adult vs embryonic roles. Peer reviewers also find this SUPPORTED without challenge, consistent with the active inhibition model.

Both address negative results with ligand over-expression (C61). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED but acknowledges uncertainty about mechanisms. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, suggesting experiments combining inhibitor knockdown with ligand over-expression to test whether negative regulators override ligand effects.

Both evaluate PTEN's mechanism (C51). OpenEval finds the inference SUPPORTED though direct demonstration is lacking. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, noting lack of evidence that PTEN promotes EGFR degradation in hub cells and suggesting additional pathways may be involved.

Both address the model of germ cells as ligand source (C81-C84). OpenEval finds this UNCERTAIN and largely speculative with indirect evidence. Peer reviewers find this UNSUPPORTED, stating insufficient evidence to localize EGF source to germ cells and requesting compound ablation experiments.
Both address biological context and background (C1-C3, C10-C18). Both evaluations find this SUPPORTED by appropriate citations and prior work. Strong concordance on foundational claims.

Both address established EGFR signaling knowledge from literature (C19-C27, C43, C47, C56-C58, C79-C80, C95-C103). Both find this SUPPORTED by appropriate citations. Strong concordance on background information.
Both address comparative examples from literature (C86-C88). Both find this SUPPORTED by appropriate citations, providing broader context for the findings. Strong concordance.

OpenEval evaluates speculation about other pathways (C78) as UNCERTAIN but reasonable given incomplete recovery block. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers do question pathway specificity elsewhere.

OpenEval R1 includes C36 (negative results for other RTKs supporting EGFR specificity). Peer R11 questions these negative results, noting they are alluded to but not shown, requesting summary of genes/pathways tested as a resource.
OpenEval R1 includes control experiments C28-C29 establishing baseline. Peer R15 accepts these controls as SUPPORTED without challenge, validating the experimental system.
OpenEval R2 includes C39 (G-TRACE control). Peer R16 accepts this control as SUPPORTED, validating the lineage tracing system for detecting transdifferentiation.
